symptom: `mxcli diff-local --ref main...feature-branch` (documented as "changes since common ancestor") printed `Warning: failed to read .feature version of mprcontents/…: exit status 128` for every unit and `Summary: 0 new, 0 modified, 0 deleted`
cause: parseRefRange split on the first "..", so "a...b" became base "a", target ".b"; `git diff --name-status a...b` listed the right files, but every `git show .b:./path` failed. It also read the old side at a, where `git diff a...b` compares against the merge base
insight: Two independent defects hide behind one symptom: the split (".b") fails loudly, and the obvious fix — split on "..." and read the old side at a — would pass any test whose branches did not diverge, then show main's own later changes reversed in every hunk. Only a repo where BOTH branches change the same unit after the split tells merge-base from a: assert the old side's size (x → feat is 1 → 4 chars; main's value would give 7 → 4). Resolve the range once (git merge-base, in the project directory) rather than per unit, and treat an empty side as HEAD the way git does (`a..` read the index through `git show :./path`). Repro: the pedapp git copy with a feature branch and a diverging master.
